## Request Signature (RS)

Single writer for approved → out-for-signature, following the Contract block’s own transition map: counterparties never see unapproved text. Stamps `signatureStatus: pending`, the request date (local calendar day), and the carrying provider.

### Example

Natural target: the linked MSA — Northwind (already signed; running against it demonstrates the guard).

### Non-goals

No e-signature API integration — this records that the request went out, so the pipeline can hold the contract accountable.

### Desk-spec extension (2026-09-02)

When the contract carries `signatureBlocks`, the request goes out ONE LINE AT A TIME in `signingOrder`: from `approved` it sends line 1; from `out for signature` it sends the next pending line whose predecessors have all signed. Every call re-runs the authority check (`Signatory.canSign` via `verifyCeremony`) against current data and refuses with per-line reasons. Order violations are therefore impossible, not merely discouraged. Contracts without blocks keep the original single-step behaviour.
